description.from: The user authorized actual installation and testing across the active project estate. Codex owns execution; planning is complete but installations are not yet claimed complete. Inspect each project and existing coordination claims, effective hooks path, custom policy, runtime and shared worktrees, then preserve or compose existing hooks and run synthetic clean/sensitive/error tests. Coordinate active Papyrus and Claude-owned work before touching their shared hooks; those projects are now in scope rather than automatically deferred. Coordinate BotSpy with its separate readiness owner. Record verified per-project results locally without publishing private policy, machine inventory, or sensitive findings. Do not globally replace hooks.
description.to: Actual local installation and validation are complete for all 137 eligible repositories with empty hook locations: one pilot, 115 in the initial batch, one refreshed coordinated installation, and 20 coordinated installations. All 137 distinct repositories preserved project state, accepted clean synthetic commits and blocked sensitive fixtures without changing the temporary test HEAD on rejection. An initial state-drift skip was safely replanned and subsequently passed. Three repositories using hook managers need 17 checkout-specific adapters that preserve configured hook paths and existing hooks; the current installer cannot safely compose them unchanged. Required project issue/branch workflows, unavailable project-tracker tooling and active-owner coordination remain prerequisites. No manager hook changes were attempted or denied. Forty-four generated/vendor/upstream repositories were excluded and eleven dangling Git pointers remain unresolved. These aggregates describe completed versus pending scope; private inventory and policy remain local. Public package release is separately pending and does not invalidate the verified local installations.
